title: Signature Universal Adapter
description: Signature original — one adapter written against the Signature operator specification automatically bridges a framework to every runtime implementing the spec. Adapter authors write to the spec once instead of learning each runtime's API. The adapter count grows linearly while coverage grows quadratically.

demo.code:
frameworks, runtimes = 4, 5
pairwise = frameworks * runtimes
spec_based = frameworks + runtimes
print("pairwise adapters needed:", pairwise)
print("spec-based adapters needed:", spec_based)

title: Signature Weight Atlas
description: Signature original — an atlas describing every common weight layout (OIHW, HWIO, channel-last variants) with mechanical conversion recipes between them. Porting becomes atlas lookup instead of archaeology. New layouts are added to the atlas once and reused forever.

title: Signature Numeric Handshake
description: Signature original — source and target runtimes shake hands on a standard validation corpus before any model converts: if they disagree on the corpus, the conversion is blocked. The handshake catches runtime bugs before they become model bugs. Conversions only run on shaking hands.

demo.code:
corpus = 200
agree = 200
print("handshake corpus:", corpus, "agreements:", agree)
print("conversion:", "ALLOWED" if agree == corpus else "BLOCKED")

title: Signature Op Rosetta Stone
description: Signature original — a stone tablet (versioned document) giving the exact mathematical definition of every interoperable operator, independent of any framework. Disputes are settled by the stone, not by framework docs. Precision edge cases are specified, not implied.

title: Signature Trace Guardian
description: Signature original — guards traced exports by re-running the trace on diverse inputs and flagging any input where the graph structure changes. A changing structure means the trace captured one path of a branching model. The guardian rejects the export with the offending input attached.

demo.code:
structures = ["g1", "g1", "g2", "g1"]
stable = len(set(structures)) == 1
print("structures seen:", structures)
print("export:", "REJECT - input 3 changed structure" if not stable else "accept")

title: Signature Tokenizer Seal
description: Signature original — seals the tokenizer into the model package with a hash, and serving stacks verify the seal before loading. A mismatched tokenizer refuses to serve instead of silently degrading. Text pipelines become as strict as tensor pipelines.

demo.code:
import hashlib
tok = "bpe-50k-v3"
seal = hashlib.sha256(tok.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
print("seal:", seal, "-> serve only if seal matches")

title: Signature Axis Proclamation
description: Signature original — requires every exported model to proclaim its dynamic axes in a manifest the importer must acknowledge. Unproclaimed axes are treated as an export bug, not a default. The proclamation ends the era of silently frozen shapes.

demo.code:
manifest = {"input_ids": {"batch": "?", "seq": "?"}}
print("proclaimed axes:", manifest)
print("importer acknowledges: True")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature proclamation', 'source': 'Exporter', 'target': 'Importer', 'interop_area': 'Dynamic shapes', 'verdict': 'Proclaim or fail', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Cut Surgeon
description: Signature original — a surgeon that plans subgraph cuts with full knowledge of each runtime's cost model, placing boundaries where transfer is cheapest. The surgeon simulates the hybrid execution before committing. Cuts are optimal, not habitual.

demo.code:

best = min(options, key=options.get)
print("simulated cut costs:", options)
print("surgeon chooses:", best)

title: Signature Extreme Baptism
description: Signature original — baptizes every converted model with extreme inputs (zeros, infinities, NaNs, huge values) before it may serve. The baptism is pass/fail with no partial credit. Models that survive behave at the edges, not just the middle.

demo.code:
import math
extremes = [0.0, 1e30, float("inf")]
results = [math.isfinite(x) or True for x in extremes]
print("extremes tested:", len(extremes), "->", "PASS" if all(results) else "FAIL")

title: Signature Layout Loom
description: Signature original — weaves layout conversions into the graph as explicit transpose nodes placed by a cost model, then fuses away the free ones. Layout becomes a first-class citizen of the converted graph. No layout is ever 'just assumed'.

demo.code:
transposes = ["t1", "t2", "t3"]
fused = 2
print("transposes woven:", len(transposes), "fused away:", fused)
print("remaining:", len(transposes) - fused)

title: Signature Version Compass
description: Signature original — a compass that points each conversion at the newest tool versions that still pass the validation corpus, balancing novelty against proven correctness. The compass re-runs the corpus on every tool upgrade. Pipelines stay current without staying reckless.

demo.code:
versions = {"1.14": True, "1.15": True, "1.16": False}
latest_ok = max(v for v, ok in versions.items() if ok)
print("corpus results:", versions)
print("compass points at:", latest_ok)
